table.title: Additional entries specific to a trap network annotation
table.source_location: physical 842 / printed 827; prerequisite §14.11.6.2 text and its LastModified/Version alternatives begin physical 841 / printed 826
table.errata: Direct inspection of the annotation arrays on physical pages 841 and 842 found only link annotations; no corrective StrikeOut/Caret overlay changes Table 403. EC3 errata inventory has no operative change to these cells.

features.actor_and_scope: Producer dictionary constraint for this legacy annotation subtype. The reader branches on Subtype to select the stored-appearance path; it does not validate this field's conformity.

features.table_rule: Date/time of the trap network's latest modification. Required if Version and AnnotStates are absent; absent if both are present.
features.actor_and_scope: Alternative writer-maintained freshness metadata. §14.11.6.2 says if the Page LastModified date is newer, the network is invalid and 'shall be regenerated'; the sentence is passive and does not itself name the actor.

features.table_rule: Required if AnnotStates is present; absent if LastModified is present. Unordered array of objects present when traps were generated that could affect page appearance, including page Contents streams, non-procedure-set page resources, non-procedure-set resources of page Form XObjects, and OPI dictionaries.
features.actor_and_scope: Producer-side snapshot used by a writer generating new traps: §14.11.6.2 explicitly says that writer verifies referenced objects against current contents. The OPI inclusion is marked deprecated in PDF 2.0.

features.table_rule: Required if Version is present; absent if LastModified is present. Names list annotation /AS values in page Annots order, excluding the TrapNet annotation itself. Entries should be null where an annotation has no /AS.
features.actor_and_scope: Version-array companion for a trap-generating workflow. The 'should be null' clause is a recommendation; table presence/absence conditions and ordering are the producer-side rules.

features.table_rule: Optional array of fonts substituted during generation of the page's trap networks.
features.actor_and_scope: Describes trap production provenance; no reader/rendering instruction is stated for it.

features.table_rule: The wider §14.11.6.2 rule requires at most one TrapNet annotation per page, last in Annots, with a stored normal appearance and Print+ReadOnly flags; PDF 2.0 deprecates the feature.
features.actor_and_scope: These are producer constraints plus an observable compatibility-reader stored-AP path. The renderer iterates Annots in document order; it does not reject multiple entries or reorder a malformed page.

code: crates/pdf-model/src/annotation.rs dispatches TrapNet as a supported stored-appearance annotation
crates/pdf-model/src/appearance.rs refuses to invent TrapNet artwork when the required stored appearance is absent
crates/pdf-model/src/content/annotations.rs renders annotations in Annots iteration order
current_consumer.table_fields: No runtime consumer was found for Table 403 LastModified, Version, AnnotStates, or FontFauxing. Grep hits are source comments/ledger rationale, not parsing or freshness decisions.

assertions.what_it_proves: A conforming stored-AP TrapNet with named /N state and /AS paints the expected red pixel in both View and Print; the fixture has a LastModified date.
assertions.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not compare LastModified with Page LastModified or parse Version, AnnotStates, or FontFauxing.

assertions.what_it_proves: Red/blue normal appearance alternatives selected by /AS render the independent literal pixel in View and Print.
assertions.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not exercise Table 403 freshness tracking.

assertions.what_it_proves: The generic test protects subtype dispatch/catch-all reporting only; it is not the behavioral visual assertion. The two viewer-core tests above are the direct rendering evidence.
assertions.what_it_does_not_prove: None of the cited/runtime assertions witnesses Table 403 field parsing or freshness policy; those fields are not a current reader feature.

scope_limits: Trap generation and regeneration are not implemented; do not treat missing prepress construction as a reader defect.

The standard explicitly addresses verification to a PDF writer generating a new trap network, but the later passive regeneration sentence omits its actor. This review leaves that textual ambiguity open and does not infer mandatory reader reporting.
A stale-metadata fixture with intentionally inconsistent dates would not be a valid-producer positive control; no conformance-failure test is drafted.
The clause is deprecated in PDF 2.0 and the reader's tested support is compatibility rendering of supplied appearances, not press-specific trapping or physical output.
